content.text:
I've submitted **index 22** (Cu 0.128, Fe 0.114, V 0.759) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 3.6e-7 A. I can't tell how close that is to the best in the library, because only three of the 297 compositions were measured.

The library is a Cu-Fe-V oxide spread measured under 2.4 eV light, and the merit budget was 3 measurements. I chose them as follows:

| Index | Cu / Fe / V | Photocurrent (A) | Why I picked it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 120 | 0.24 / 0.30 / 0.46 | 2.6e-7 | Near the Cu₃Fe₄(VO₄)₆ ratio (3:4:6), which I remembered from the literature as a candidate photoanode |
| **22** | 0.13 / 0.11 / 0.76 | **3.6e-7** | Middle of the V-rich area where the library is most densely sampled |
| 14 | 0.09 / 0.09 / 0.82 | 2.9e-7 | Tests whether even more V helps; it didn't |

- **Likely best region:** the results point to a local peak around V ≈ 0.75 with Cu and Fe near 0.1 each. With only three points this is a guess.
- **Unexplored:** the Cu-rich side (Cu above about 0.4) and the Fe-rich side (Fe above about 0.4) were never measured.
- **Model suggestion not used:** the Gaussian-process model's pick (index 32) predicted about 1.6e-7 A, below what I had already measured, so I spent the last measurement on index 14 instead.
- **Unused tools:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so no phases were identified. The list of known crystal structures was too large to display, so I didn't look at it either.
